title: Fabricate a flareless-fitting-tube connection
subject: General
assumptions: The sleeve is oriented with its cutting edge and pilot facing the tube end that will enter the fitting.
The fitting body is clamped in the vise so it cannot rotate, with jaws off the threads and sealing cone.
The tube axis is coaxial with the fitting, not cocked or side-loaded, with the nut hand-started straight.
The tube is bottomed firmly against the seat in the fitting before the nut is tightened.
The sleeve grip point is found by turning the tube back and forth while tightening until it no longer turns.
At completion the tube can no longer be rotated by hand within the sleeve.
openQuestions: Every check, error mode and evidence item in this pack was drafted by packs/compile_pack.py from the procedure sheet and handbook, and has not been reviewed by a subject-matter expert.

The AIM procedure sheet documents no steps for 'Preset the Sleeve', 'Inspect the Preset Connection', yet the task title and the sheet's own equipment list call for that work. Those steps were drafted from the handbook and the reference video and carry `origin: drafted`. Confirm with AIM whether they form part of the graded submission, and ask for a corrected procedure sheet if they do.
Verify the fraction rendered as "1-1/6" against the source FAA-H-8083-30B PDF (1-1/8 and 1-1/16 are both plausible) before any turn-count criterion is graded.
Confirm with an SME whether presetting and post-preset inspection are in scope for AM.I.D.S8 at all, since the AIM sheet's step list ends at 'Deburr the tubing ends'.
Fix the tube material and outside diameter used in the exercise, and require students to state them, or neither the turn range nor the clearance limit can be selected.
Resolve whether the 0.015" limit applies to 'steel' (p. 9-6 body) or 'corrosion-resistant steel' (Fig. 9-14 caption, p. 9-8) tubing.

checks.text: The marked length matches the length required for the assembly, including fitting engagement allowance.
checks.src: Handbook p.9-6: "Cut the tube to the correct length"; procedure sheet step 1 requires measuring needed length.

checks.text: The layout mark is a single crisp line encircling the tube perpendicular to its axis.
checks.src: Sheet note 1: "Align the marked line and sharp cutting wheel precisely"; handbook p.9-6 "with the ends perfectly square."

checks.text: The required length is established from the applicable drawing, manual or routing data before marking.

checks.text: The scale is zeroed flush against the tube end with no slack or parallax when the mark is struck.
checks.src: Measuring technique implied by step 1; only observable while the measurement is being taken.

errors.text: Tube marked short, so the finished tube cannot bottom firmly in the fitting seat.
Mark laid out at an angle or not carried around the tube, guaranteeing a non-square cut.
Multiple or smeared trial marks left on the tube, obscuring the intended cut line.

checks.text: The cut end is square to the tube axis within a squareness check against a machinist square.
checks.src: Handbook: "Cut the tube to the correct length, with the ends perfectly square." Sheet states only "Cut the tubing."

checks.text: Finished tube length matches the length measured and marked in step 1.
checks.src: Sheet: "Measure needed length of tubing"; handbook: "Cut the tube to the correct length."

checks.text: The tube at and near the cut shows no flattening, ovality or crush marks from the cutting wheel.
checks.src: Sheet directs the wheel be tightened only "slightly snug" and re-tightened progressively, which prevents pinching the tube.

checks.text: The end is severed cleanly with no torn, ragged or partially broken-off metal or multiple off-track cut grooves.
checks.src: Sheet: "Continue re-tightening and rotating the cutting tool until cleanly cut through tubing."

errors.text: Cutting wheel over-tightened, ovalizing or partially collapsing the tube at the cut.
End cut noticeably out of square, so the tube cannot bottom squarely on the fitting seat.
Wheel wanders off the mark, leaving spiral or double cut tracks and a torn end.
Cut to the wrong length relative to the mark.

checks.text: Both the inside and outside edges of the tube end are free of raised burrs and ragged metal.
checks.src: Handbook p.9-6: "Deburr the inside and outside of the tube"; sheet note 2 requires inside diameter smooth.

checks.text: The bore at the deburred end measures the original inside diameter, with no bell-mouthing or wall thinning.
checks.src: Sheet note 2: "check the inside diameter is smooth and the original size returned"; handbook is silent on any dimension.

checks.text: The tube end remains perpendicular to the tube axis after deburring and sanding.
checks.src: Handbook p.9-6: "Cut the tube to the correct length, with the ends perfectly square"; squareness must survive deburring.

checks.text: No metal chips, swarf or abrasive grit remain inside the tube bore or on the end face.
checks.src: Implied by sanding with lubricated paper and by contamination risk; handbook states no cleanliness requirement here.

errors.text: Over-deburring bells or thins the tube end, so the sleeve cannot grip sound wall at presetting.
Abrasive grit or metal chips left in the bore and carried into the system.
Inside burr left in place, restricting flow and visible as a ragged lip in the bore.
Outside edge left sharp or scratched by sandpaper, marring the sleeve seating area.

steps.text: Slip the nut, then the sleeve, over the tube and lubricate the fitting and nut threads with hydraulic fluid.

checks.text: The nut is on the tube first, behind the sleeve, so the sleeve sits between the nut and the tube end.
checks.src: Handbook p.9-6: "Slip the nut, then the sleeve, over the tube (step 1)"; procedure sheet states the same order.

checks.text: The sleeve is oriented with its cutting edge and pilot facing the tube end that will enter the fitting.
checks.src: Figure 9-14 labels "Sleeve pilot"/"Sleeve cutting edge" toward the fitting; drafted supplemental step, needs subject-matter confirmation.

checks.text: The tube end is cut square to the tube axis and free of burrs inside and outside before the nut and sleeve go on.
checks.src: Handbook p.9-6: "Cut the tube to the correct length, with the ends perfectly square. Deburr the inside and outside of the tube." Squareness needs a square/gauge.

checks.text: Hydraulic fluid is applied to the threads of both the fitting and the nut before assembly.
checks.src: Handbook p.9-6: "lubricate the threads of the fitting and nut with hydraulic fluid"; sheet safety note warns dry sleeves cause stress cracks.

errors.text: Sleeve slipped on backwards, cutting edge facing away from the fitting, so it cannot bite the tube.
Nut and fitting threads assembled dry, risking galling and stress cracking of the sleeve.
Sleeve installed before the nut, so the nut cannot be drawn onto the fitting.
Nut and sleeve installed over an out-of-square or burred tube end, now hidden under the sleeve.

steps.text: Place the fitting in a vise and hold the tube firmly and squarely on the fitting seat so it bottoms in the fitting.

checks.text: The fitting body is clamped in the vise so it cannot rotate, with jaws off the threads and sealing cone.
checks.src: Handbook: "Place the fitting in a vise (step 2)"; the jaw-placement detail is inferred and this step is supplemental, so SME confirmation is needed.

checks.text: The tube axis is coaxial with the fitting, not cocked or side-loaded, with the nut hand-started straight.
checks.src: Handbook: "hold the tubing firmly and squarely on the seat in the fitting"; step is supplemental and unreviewed by an SME.

checks.text: The tube is bottomed firmly against the seat in the fitting before the nut is tightened.
checks.src: Handbook: "(The tube must bottom firmly in the fitting.)" Seating cannot be seen once assembled; supplemental step, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The sleeve grip point is found by turning the tube back and forth while tightening until it no longer turns.
checks.src: Handbook: "slowly turn the tube back and forth while tightening the nut. When the tube no longer turns, the nut is ready for tightening."

errors.text: Nut tightened before the tube is bottomed on the seat, presetting the sleeve at the wrong location on the tube.
Tube held cocked in the fitting, so the sleeve cutting edge bites unevenly around the tube circumference.
Vise jaws clamped on the fitting threads or sealing cone, marring the sealing surface.

steps.text: Tighten the nut until the cutting edge of the sleeve grips the tube, turning the tube back and forth while tightening until it no longer turns.

checks.text: At completion the tube can no longer be rotated by hand within the sleeve.
checks.src: Handbook: "slowly turn the tube back and forth while tightening the nut. When the tube no longer turns, the nut is ready for tightening." Supplemental step, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: Tube stays bottomed firmly and squarely on the fitting seat throughout nut tightening.
checks.src: Handbook: "hold the tubing firmly and squarely on the seat in the fitting. (The tube must bottom firmly in the fitting.)" Provisional supplemental step.

checks.text: Nut is stopped at the grip point, with no final-tightening turns yet applied.
checks.src: Handbook separates grip point from step 3: "the nut is ready for tightening"; final turns are a distinct operation. Provisional.

checks.text: Tube is coaxial with the fitting and nut, not cocked or offset at the junction.
checks.src: Rests on handbook "firmly and squarely on the seat in the fitting"; squareness is visible at the joint. Provisional supplemental step.

errors.text: Nut run down well past the grip point, over-presetting the sleeve while the joint still looks normal.
Tube not held bottomed in the seat, so the sleeve bites with the tube unseated or cocked.
Tube never rotated during tightening, so the grip point is guessed rather than found.

steps.text: Final-tighten the nut the number of turns specified for the tube material and outside diameter.

checks.text: Nut is turned the specified amount past the grip point: 1 to 1-1/6 turns for aluminum alloy up to 1/2" OD, 1-1/6 to 1-1/2 turns for steel or aluminum over 1/2" OD.
checks.src: Handbook: "tighten the nut from 1 to 11/6 turns... tighten from 11/6 to 11/2 turns"; step is supplemental, and the fraction is typographically suspect.

checks.text: Turn count is taken from the point at which the tube no longer turns, not from finger-tight or first thread contact.
checks.src: Handbook: "When the tube no longer turns, the nut is ready for tightening." Reference point only evidenced by watching the tightening.

checks.text: Tube material and outside diameter are identified so the correct turn range can be selected.
checks.src: Supplemental note: "tube material and outside diameter must be known before this step can be graded"; provisional, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: Finished connection shows the nut drawn down squarely on the fitting body with the tube axially aligned and no wrench galling or rounded flats.
checks.src: Workmanship expectation for the completed preset; supplemental section, not SME reviewed.

errors.text: Nut final-tightened less than the specified turns, so the sleeve never fully bites and the joint can blow off while looking correctly assembled.
Nut tightened past the maximum turns, over-deforming or collapsing the tube and setting up line failure.
Turns counted from finger-tight instead of from the grip point, giving an out-of-range preset that must be redone with a new sleeve.
Wrench slippage marks, galling or rounded corners on the B-nut or fitting hex.

subtasks.label: Inspect the Preset Connection
subtasks.excluded: 2 [document], 2 [measurement], 2 [video] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

steps.text: Disconnect the tubing from the fitting.

checks.text: The tube assembly is fully separated from the fitting, with the nut backed off and the tube end free.
checks.src: Handbook: "After presetting the sleeve, disconnect the tubing from the fitting and check the following points"; disassembly is prerequisite to inspection.

checks.text: The preset sleeve remains on the tube in its swaged position, not slid off or removed with the nut.
checks.src: Drafted supplemental step; preset evidence is destroyed if sleeve is displaced. Inference needs subject-matter confirmation.

checks.text: Tube end, sleeve pilot and nut/fitting threads show no gouging, galling or cross-threading from disassembly.
checks.src: Supplemental step drafted from p.9-6 presetting sequence; handbook states no damage standard for disassembly. Needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: Tube material and outside diameter are recorded so the correct pilot-clearance limit can be applied in later checks.
checks.src: Handbook: "maximum clearance of 0.005" for aluminum alloy tubing or 0.015" for steel tubing" — limit depends on material/OD.

errors.text: Nut is re-tightened or the joint reassembled and snugged before inspection, adding turns and over-swaging the sleeve.
Tube is pulled or twisted out while the nut is still partially tight, bending the tube or shifting the sleeve pilot.
Sleeve is stripped off or pushed along the tube during disassembly, destroying the preset evidence.

steps.text: Verify the tube extends 3/32" to 1/8" beyond the sleeve pilot.

checks.text: The tube end protrudes beyond the sleeve pilot by 3/32" to 1/8" as measured with a rule or caliper.
checks.src: Handbook: "The tube should extend 3⁄32" to 1⁄8" beyond the sleeve pilot; otherwise, blowoff may occur." Step is supplemental; needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The tube, nut and sleeve are off the fitting with the sleeve pilot and tube end fully exposed and unobstructed.
checks.src: Handbook: "disconnect the tubing from the fitting and check the following points" — measurement is impossible with the tube seated.

checks.text: Tube visibly projects past the sleeve pilot rather than sitting flush with or recessed behind it.
checks.src: Gross condition of the handbook's "extend ... beyond the sleeve pilot" requirement; exact dimension still needs measuring.

checks.text: The extension is measured from the sleeve pilot face, with the sleeve left in its preset position and not slid along the tube.
checks.src: Supplemental sheet places this check after presetting; a repositioned sleeve invalidates the reading. Needs SME confirmation.

errors.text: Tube extends less than 3/32" (or is flush with the pilot), leaving a plausible-looking joint prone to blowoff.
Extension read from the nut face or with the sleeve shifted, producing a false in-tolerance value.
Tube extends more than 1/8" beyond the sleeve pilot.

steps.text: Verify the sleeve pilot contacts the tube or is within the maximum clearance for the tube material.

checks.text: Clearance between the sleeve pilot and the tube is zero contact, or no more than 0.005" (aluminum alloy) / 0.015" (corrosion-resistant steel).
checks.src: Handbook p.9-6: "sleeve pilot should contact the tube or have a maximum clearance of 0.005" for aluminum alloy tubing or 0.015" for steel tubing"; step is supplemental, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The tube material and outside diameter are identified so the correct clearance limit is selected.
checks.src: Supplemental step distinguishes aluminum alloy from corrosion-resistant steel limits; material data must be established from spec. Needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The pilot area of the tube shows no crack, split or gross collapse; only slight deformation at the sleeve cut is present.
checks.src: Handbook: "A slight collapse of the tube at the sleeve cut is permissible." Gross collapse or splitting invalidates the pilot contact judgement.

checks.text: Sleeve remains on the tube with the pilot region exposed and clean, so clearance can be gauged.
checks.src: Supplemental inspection step requires the disconnected tube/sleeve be presented for pilot inspection; needs SME confirmation.

errors.text: Clearance judged by eye only and never gauged, so an over-clearance pilot passes while the assembly looks normal.
Steel limit (0.015") applied to aluminum alloy tubing, accepting a pilot gap that exceeds 0.005".
Tube is cracked or grossly collapsed at the sleeve cut yet accepted as "slight deformation."

steps.text: Verify the sleeve pilot does not move on the tube except in rotation.

checks.text: The sleeve pilot resists axial sliding along the tube when hand-pressure is applied, permitting only rotation.
checks.src: Handbook p.9-6: "No movement of the sleeve pilot, except rotation, is permissible." Only an attempted push/pull shows it.

checks.text: Tube deformation at the sleeve cut is limited to a slight collapse, with no crushing, kinking or split.
checks.src: Handbook p.9-6: "A slight collapse of the tube at the sleeve cut is permissible." Step itself is supplemental, not AIM-sheet text.

checks.text: A continuous witness ring from the sleeve cutting edge is visible around the full tube circumference.
checks.src: Rests on "Tighten the nut until the cutting edge of the sleeve grips the tube"; grip evidence inferred, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The nut and sleeve remain assembled on the tube after disconnection so pilot retention can be assessed.
checks.src: Supplemental inspect section step 1 disconnects the tube from the fitting only; sleeve stays preset on tube.

errors.text: Sleeve pilot slides axially on the tube (under-preset), yet the assembly still looks correctly made.
Tube crushed, kinked or split at the sleeve cut from over-tightening the nut.
Sleeve forced with pliers or a tool during the movement check, marring the tube surface.
